comments.text:
I have used Airbnb quite a bit and still use them. However, I do a lot of work on the front end.
I only stay in places that have a lot of positive reviews (in the 4.9 range or higher) and the host also has to be highly rated. I will usually reach out to the host to ask a question to check their communication and response time. I use Google Maps to look at the neighborhood and make sure there is some sort of free cancellation with the reservation. If it doesn’t have those things, I don’t book.
I really like Airbnb for international stays. Those a lot of times are cheaper than hotels and give you more space. Especially if you are staying for an extended period.
I like Airbnb but I also do the work and the research to make sure I know what I am getting.

comments.author: @Eaglejake
comments.text: Ok, I'm only 2 minutes in.....Fact:  You are paying a cleaning fee for Hotels as well.  Airbnbs can range from 400 square foot condos, up to 4000 square foot homes, the acreage around the property, including pools/hot tubs.  You spend one night, or one week in a house, and there is going to be a lot of cleaning, inside and outside, to prepare for the next guest.  Our Airbnb is marketed as "Pet Friendly".  Half the time the guests don't pick up the poop, or take it to the garbage can outside.  Some Airbnb's are managed by owners that do not live across the street, and the next guest is not scheduled for 10 days, hence leaving the A/C at 75 or above, so the A/C doesn't freeze for 10 days at 68 degrees, or taking the garbage out of the kitchen.  Finally, hotels don't make money on overnight stays....they make them with conventions and conferences.  There are advantages and disadvantages to each.  Short term rentals have been around forever......"chores"?......."running a business".....yea, not year round, and "cleaning" is cleaning a house, which is different from a hotel room, that includes a bed and a small bath.  Three sides to every argument.
